items.title: 油库成了战场：也门冲突开始碰到沙特的能源神经
items.brief: 导弹在利雅得附近被拦截，沙特同时打击也门油库，能源设施和民航的风险都在往上走。

en.title: Oil depots are now part of the battlefield in Yemen’s war
en.brief: Missiles were intercepted near Riyadh as Saudi Arabia struck fuel depots in Yemen, putting energy sites and air travel under more pressure.
en.take: Saudi Arabia said Houthi forces launched missiles toward the area where Saudi Aramco’s headquarters is located, with interceptions reported near Riyadh. Saudi forces then struck strategic fuel facilities near Yemen’s capital. This is more than another exchange of fire: when depots, airports and oil-company areas become targets, oil supply, flight schedules and security costs across the Gulf all become more fragile. There is no sign of a broad supply disruption yet; the key question is whether attacks spread to export terminals, refineries or shipping routes.

en.title: A Kyiv power plant is hit—and Ukraine says warnings came too late
en.brief: Beyond the blackout risk, Ukraine is questioning whether missile-warning support from allies is becoming less dependable.
en.take: Russia struck a key power plant in Kyiv, while President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said allies had not warned Ukraine in advance of Russian ballistic-missile attacks. Together, the claims raise more than a repair problem: Ukraine is approaching the heating season and can ill afford further damage to its grid. Any gap in warning or intelligence sharing gives civilians less time to shelter and makes air defence more difficult. The accounts still need independent verification, but they put the reliability of wartime support in plain view.

items.brief: 增长虽然没有立刻熄火，但贸易摩擦、债务和地缘冲突叠在一起，缓冲空间正在变薄。

en.title: The IMF says the global economy is nearing its shock limit
en.brief: Growth has not collapsed, but trade friction, debt and conflict are thinning the cushion that kept the world economy steady.
en.take: The International Monetary Fund warned in its latest World Economic Outlook that the global economy could soon test the limits of its resilience. That does not mean a worldwide recession starts tomorrow. It means the buffers that have held up jobs, spending and policy responses now face trade barriers, war-related disruption and heavy debt at the same time. For households, the path is usually gradual rather than dramatic: pricier imported goods, borrowing costs that stay sticky, and employers becoming more cautious about hiring and investment.

items.title: 欧盟给中国混动车设进口上限，车价选择可能一起变少
items.brief: 一年35万辆的上限不只是在谈贸易，欧洲消费者以后能买到什么车、多少钱买，都会受影响。
items.take: 欧盟计划将中国混合动力汽车的年进口量限制在35万辆。这种做法比单纯加关税更直接：它先限定能进来的车数，再由车企和经销商决定把配额留给哪些车型和市场。欧洲想给本土制造商留空间，但竞争较少也可能让消费者少一些价格较低的选择。中国车企则可能加快在欧洲本地组装，或者把资源转向其他市场。

en.title: Europe caps Chinese hybrid imports, and car choice could get tighter
en.brief: The 350,000-a-year ceiling is not just a trade measure: it could shape which cars Europeans can buy and what they pay.
en.take: The EU plans to limit imports of Chinese hybrid vehicles to 350,000 a year. This is more direct than a tariff: it fixes the number of cars that can enter, leaving manufacturers and dealers to decide which models and markets receive the scarce slots. Europe wants to give domestic producers room, but less competition can also mean fewer lower-priced choices for buyers. Chinese carmakers may respond by assembling more vehicles inside Europe or shifting resources to other markets.

en.title: An alleged recording device at OpenAI shows how AI competition is turning into an intelligence problem
en.brief: A Saudi man has been charged over an alleged sophisticated recording device in an OpenAI office; model companies are guarding more than code.
en.take: The BBC reports that a Saudi man has been charged with planting a “sophisticated” recording device in an OpenAI office. The case remains an allegation before the courts, not a proven account. But it highlights a reality of frontier AI: hiring plans, model roadmaps, commercial deals and safety debates can all be valuable intelligence. It will not change a chatbot overnight, but it gives corporate customers, researchers and governments more reason to scrutinize who can access models, data and internal decisions.

en.title: Apple’s trade-secrets fight reaches OpenAI’s hiring files
en.brief: A judge ordered OpenAI to hand over hiring records; the question is not just who left Apple, but whether confidential material travelled with them.
en.take: A US judge ordered OpenAI to turn over hiring records in Apple’s trade-secrets dispute. A court order is not a finding that OpenAI broke the law, but it moves the case into an evidence-heavy phase. Fierce competition for AI talent makes job moves routine. The sensitive question is whether a new employer encouraged, received or used confidential information from a former employer. If the case broadens, technology firms may impose stricter hiring, onboarding and project-separation procedures.

en.brief: Muse Wonder matters less as a benchmark claim than as a model Meta can place inside social, creative and developer tools.
en.take: Meta released Muse Wonder, described as its first frontier model. Public detail remains limited: capabilities, pricing, availability and safety limits need fuller documentation. Meta controls enormous consumer-product entry points; if the model is integrated into its apps and developer tools, people may encounter it while posting, messaging, creating or using advertising tools rather than choosing a separate AI app. For developers, actual access terms and cost will matter more than a claim to be the strongest.

items.title: 东南亚毒霾又来了：污染不认国界，孩子和户外工作者先受罪
items.brief: 跨境烟霾让呼吸变难，也再次暴露出一个老问题：烧起来很快，跨国追责却很慢。

en.title: Southeast Asia’s toxic haze is back, and children and outdoor workers pay first
en.brief: Cross-border smoke makes breathing harder and exposes an old failure: fires spread quickly, but accountability moves slowly.
en.take: The BBC examined who is responsible for toxic haze in Southeast Asia, where smoke from wildfires and land clearing can cross national borders. For city residents, this is not an abstract environmental issue. Poor air quality hits children, older people, people with asthma and outdoor workers first, while schools, flights and daily travel can also be disrupted. The hard part is that landowners, fire sources and regulators may sit in different regions or countries; responding only after smoke reaches cities is already too late.

en.title: Google Play lets anyone make a private app—and shifts more safety checking to the user
en.brief: You may not need to code to build an Android tool for yourself, but private distribution does not make its permissions or data use safe by default.
en.take: Google Play now supports private Android apps built through “vibe coding”: users describe what they want in plain language and AI helps generate the code and app. It lowers the barrier to making a budgeting tool, file organizer or household utility. But it also returns part of the testing and security judgment to the user. A private app may not have faced the same long public scrutiny as a widely distributed one. If it asks for contacts, photos, location or payment access, being “made for me” is not a reason to trust it automatically.

items.brief: 德国审理一名被控参与破坏北溪管道的乌克兰人，案件会重新碰触战争、能源和盟友关系的敏感线。

en.title: The Nord Stream case goes to trial, reopening Europe’s energy-security wound
en.brief: Germany is trying a Ukrainian accused over the Nord Stream sabotage, reviving difficult questions about war, energy and allies.
en.take: Germany has begun the trial of a Ukrainian accused of involvement in the sabotage of the Nord Stream gas pipelines. This is not a final account of what happened: the defendant has the right to challenge the evidence, and the allegation must be tested in court. But the explosions remain one of Europe’s most sensitive wartime mysteries. They damaged more than pipelines, deepening anxiety about energy dependence and protection of critical infrastructure. If the trial reveals more about the operation, financing or helpers, it could add political strain between Germany, Ukraine and Ukraine’s supporters.
